§9.4.1 Gutter Columns

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-gutter-columns · tables columns currency

✅ Normative

A currency glyph or a separator typeset in a column track of its own SHOULD be rendered in the same cell as the value it belongs to — $ 277.09, $1,200 — $1,800. A marker numeral such as (i) or (ii) SHOULD be rendered in a column of its own.

Financial PDFs frequently typeset $ in its own column track, and print ranges as value — value with the dash in a track of its own. Those tracks are real in the typesetting, but they are layout, not data.

Printed tracks:  $ | 1,200 | — | $ | 1,800
Rendered as:     $1,200 — $1,800   (one cell)

Currency and separators: merged into the value

  • A currency glyph printed in its own track SHOULD be rendered in the cell of the number it belongs to. The glyph MUST NOT be dropped: where the page prints $ only on some rows, only those rows' values carry it.
  • A separator between the two ends of a range (a dash, +/-, to) SHOULD be rendered in one cell with both ends.
  • A $ kept in a cell of its own beside its value, as a pair of cells, also conforms; the single cell is the preferred form.

✅ Sample — warn

$ typeset in its own column track, separate from the digits, throughout the balance sheet. It is printed only on the first row of each block and on the grand total, so only those values carry it. The stub header is italic. The row labels are printed flush left, without indentation, so every label is level 0.

❌ Counter-sample — some

The $ sits in its own boxed column track in the image, which looks like a column of its own. It is not: the glyph belongs to the value, so the first value cell reads $274. The Second Quarter and January - June spanners printed above the header are part of the table.

Marker gutters: kept as a column

| (i)  | Base salary … |     ← one column for the numeral, one for the text
| (ii) | Bonus …       |

A marker numeral such as (i) / (ii) SHOULD be rendered in a column of its own. A merged (i) Base salary … cell also conforms, but the separate numeral column is the preferred form.

Why the two resolve opposite ways

A currency symbol is part of the value. A marker numeral is a reference label: it is cited elsewhere on the page ("see (ii)"), so it has an identity of its own and earns a column.

A gutter this rule does not name is decided by the column-count test: a track gets its own column only if a competent person modelling this data in a spreadsheet would give it one. That is the same appeal to how a person would model the content that decides Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 — judge by the data, not by what is inked.

✅ Sample — an operator in its own track

The Outlook table prints $5.70 Billion | +/- | $300 Million as three ruled cells, and 1.26 Billion spanning all three on the last row. The +/- track is the range dash of this rule in another costume: one value, one cell. Merged, the GAAP and Non-GAAP ranges each become one column and the reconciling amount sits between them; the row labels are bold.

✅ Sample — v. in its own track

A court daily list: time, case number and party, v., the other party, hearing type. The v. column carries the same token on every row that has two parties and nothing on the rows that do not — a separator track, like the range dash, so it joins the two parties in one cell. Rows with a single In the matter of… line then take the same shape.
